name: Westendorf
kurzbeschreibung: Popular ski destination in the Wilder Kaiser ski region, featuring kilometers of downhill runs and the famous night skiing trail.
beschreibung:
Überblick

The municipality of Westendorf is situated on a sunny plateau at an altitude of 783 metres above sea level in the Brixen Valley within the Kitzbühel district of Tyrol, nestled between the gentle grassy peaks of the Kitzbühel Alps and the rugged Kaiser mountains. Home to approximately 3,700 residents and covering more than 95 square kilometres, Westendorf ranks among the largest municipalities by area in the district. This quintessential alpine village extends from its beautifully adorned historic centre deep into the secluded, 16-kilometre-long Windau Valley, which ascends towards the summit of the Kröndlhorn at 2,444 metres. Westendorf gained worldwide acclaim when it was awarded the gold medal at the prestigious Entente Florale Europe competition as 'Europe's Most Beautiful Blooming and Green Village'. The town pairs first-rate hospitality with seamless access linking SkiWelt Wilder Kaiser-Brixental and KitzSki.

Geschichte

Archaeological discoveries of cremation burial sites establish continuous human settlement on the high terrace since the Bronze and Iron Ages. The village was officially documented in 1234 when Count Otto of Wasserburg transferred local estates to Rott Abbey in Bavaria. For centuries the entire Brixen Valley belonged ecclesiastically and politically to the Prince-Archbishopric of Salzburg, only passing definitively to the Habsburg Crownland of Tyrol in 1816 following the Congress of Vienna. The parish church dedicated to Saint Nicholas was first documented in 1320, undergoing late-Gothic enlargement around 1500 and subsequent Baroque remodelling. Between 1771 and 1775, master builder Andre Hueber constructed the present late-Baroque hall church, distinguished by magnificent ceiling frescoes painted by Matthias Kirchner in 1774.

Anreise

Westendorf enjoys excellent transport links within the Kitzbühel Alps. Motorists arriving from Germany can travel toll-free via motorway A93 to Kufstein-Süd or along the Inntal Autobahn A12 exiting at Wörgl-Ost, following federal highways B178 and B170 straight into the Brixen Valley. Rail infrastructure is exemplary: the local railway station Westendorf in Tirol on the Salzburg-Tyrol line (Giselabahn) is served hourly by S-Bahn Tirol and regional express trains from the railway hub at Wörgl, providing connections to international ICE and Railjet networks. Furthermore, regional bus route 4051 links Westendorf to Hopfgarten and Kitzbühel. Visitors staying locally benefit from complimentary regional rail and bus travel with the Kitzbühel Alps Guest Card.

Tipps

In summer, the Alpenrosenbahn cable car whisks hikers and families from the village centre up to the Choralpe (1,820 m) and the 'Alpinolino' mountain adventure park featuring nature discovery trails and panoramic walkways. In winter, Westendorf serves as a premier winter sports paradise providing direct access to the vast SkiWelt Wilder Kaiser-Brixental network, the challenging 'Black Eagle' downhill run, and the renowned Boarders Playground freestyle park on the Gampenkogel. The Ki-West gondola in the Windau Valley provides a convenient connection to the KitzSki area. Nature lovers must discover the tranquil Windau Valley: an unspoilt alpine haven along the river offering gentle bike rides and rewarding hikes to traditional cheese dairies like the Gamskogelhütte. Golfers enjoy the 18-hole championship course of Golfclub Kitzbüheler Alpen.
